_readme: Where every group a hygiene hold can be read into belongs (DRE-9290). `scripts/hold_waits.py` (DRE-9274) reads each open `hyg-hand-step`, `hyg-blocker-owner` and `hand-work-overdue` hold into a group by its receipt's own words and prints it as `<kind> — <group>`; this table places each group in exactly one of three buckets. `pipeline` — the pipeline does the step and the hold ends with a receipt. `owner` — the hold goes to its real owner automatically. `operator` — it stays a hold and says why. One row per group: `kind` is the hold's tag (null for the kindless `window cut short — not read`), `group` the group as `hold_waits.py` prints it after `<kind> — `, `bucket` one of the three words, `who` who acts, and `why` one plain sentence with no `·` and no line break, because hygiene's receipt refuses both and later cards quote it into receipts. A `group` may be a template: each `<…>` part is a placeholder, and the row places every group `scripts/hold_placement.py`'s `groups()` enumerates that the template matches. `groups()` reads every group off the three writers' own vocabularies — `config/operator-step-kinds.json`, `hygiene_blockers.WAITING`, `routing_verdict`, the lane contract and the `Kind:` leads `scripts/hold_deadline.py` composes for `reconcile.py` — never off this file, and groups compare case-blind. `python3 scripts/hold_placement.py check` exits 1 on a group no row places, a row that places no group, a group placed twice, a bucket outside the three words, and a `why` a receipt would refuse; tests/test_hold_placement.py runs it, which is how CI runs it.

rows.why: A repository variable is set with the bureau App's own token, and a card the Operator Agent refuses stands with the refusal as its reason.
The branch, the file and the pull request are each an op the Operator Agent runs with the bureau App's own token, so no person's hand is needed.
A project's status is an op the Operator Agent runs, and filing a card has no op, so such a card is refused and stands with the refusal as its reason.

A script run from a checkout reaches an AWS account, a production store or a machine the pipeline holds no credential for, and the Operator Agent runs only the read-only scripts `config/operator-do.json` allows.
A deploy needs production access and the operator's AWS profile, and `config/operator-do.json` refuses it.
The card names a person acting, or no machine kind matched and it is read as a person's so nothing claims more automation than exists, and the receipt's evidence says which.

rows.who: the blocking card's owner — its assignee, else its creator, when a person (a Linear mention)
rows.why: The notice goes to the person who owns the blocking card, and a blocker with no person owner stays with the operator and its notice says so.

It is not a separate wait: the notice rides on that step and ends when the step is done, the Operator Agent takes such a card first and does a step of a kind it does, and the notice names its step's placement.
Every card it held up is closed, so nothing waits on it and the hygiene agent ends it.

The held-up cards' states did not come back from the read, so the hold-end lane names the hold as a left row in the hygiene summary on every pass it cannot decide and ends it on the first pass that reads every held-up card closed.
It is the 24-hour chase on a step that is still a person's: the card's hand-step group says why, and a step the Operator Agent does closes the card first.
